concerns.text: Task T123 ('Implement Conformational Ensemble Sampling') directly violates Spec.md Assumptions which state 'ensemble sampling is documented as future work' and 'Single lowest-Energy Conformer per molecule... is used'. This task introduces a scope violation by implementing out-of-scope functionality.

Task T122 ('Benchmark Comparison... against experimental dipole moments') violates Spec.md Assumptions ('Physical measurement validation is out of scope') and FR-011 ('physical experimental measurements are out of scope'). Implementing this task contradicts the defined ground truth standard.

Tasks T119, T120, and T125 introduce hardcoded physical constants (e.g., 'C-N bond length 1.32 Å', 'C-H: 0.4 D') and physics-informed loss terms not authorized by Spec.md FR-004 (which only requires a 'lightweight SchNet-style GNN') or Plan.md. This constitutes unauthorized scope creep and potential bias injection.

Task T016 hardcodes a subset size of '5000 molecules' and notes 'No runtime monitoring or dynamic reduction logic is used'. This violates the Plan.md Methodology which specifies 'Randomly sample [deferred] molecules' to fit memory/runtime, and risks violating FR-010 (6h runtime) if 5000 molecules exceed the compute budget on 2 vCPUs. The task silently relaxes the dynamic feasibility constraint.

Task T018 generates 'Coulomb matrices' but the Plan.md Methodology explicitly specifies 'Topological Coulomb Matrices (using graph distances)'. The task description does not reflect this specific constraint, risking a deliverable that uses standard Euclidean Coulomb matrices instead of the required Topological variant, violating the baseline comparison scope defined in the Plan.

Task T041 implements 'Wilcoxon signed-rank test' as the primary method. While the Plan.md Methodology supports this, Spec.md FR-008 and SC-004 explicitly mandate 'paired t-tests (α=0.05)'. The task silently relaxes the statistical validation requirement defined in the Spec without a documented exception or amendment to the Spec.
